review.brief: Review RM39 tier 5 (RM39-telemetry-rename-supercharger-port) - a pure identifier rename, no behavior change. Read the DIFF of commits 882f7eb (wave 1) and 64f0329 (wave 2), not the whole module. Validate: (1) MODULE BOUNDARIES - the telemetry worker edited only internal/telemetry/** plus the 4 leader-granted paths (internal/app/{app.go,processor.go,processor_test.go}, cmd/poller/main.go); internal/gateway and cmd/web are untouched. (2) SCOPE DISCIPLINE (design.md D1) - internal/gateway's Deps.SuperchargerReader (typed charging.SessionReader) and internal/analytics' fakes satisfying charging.SuperchargerSessionAnalyticsReader are DIFFERENT identifiers that must NOT have been renamed. A rename there is a blocker finding. (3) RENAME COMPLETENESS against design.md D2's name table - no half-renamed identifier, no dangling old name inside internal/telemetry. (4) NO BEHAVIOR CHANGE - no signature, SQL, schema, migration or expected-test-value differs; sqlc models.go has zero diff and query.sql.go is comment-only. (5) TEST CONTRACT (design.md) - the _test.go edits are identifier-only; assertions and expected values are byte-identical. Any weakened or deleted assertion is a blocker. (6) DOC/KB ACCURACY - internal/telemetry/AGENTS.md and the 3 kkpa/context files now record the closed state, and the tier-4 'do not fix it' instruction no longer reads as live. (7) ANTI-GAMING - no task or acceptance criterion was edited or deleted; tasks.md 43/43 reflects real state. TEST-EXECUTION-POLICY (verbatim): Claude writes tests but never runs the suite - never go test ./..., make test, make test-with-db or make check. It MAY run go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l, make build, make vet, make bins, and the standalone guards. The owner runs the suite and reports results. WHICH SIGNALS CAME FROM WHERE: go build ./..., go vet ./..., gofmt -l on the 5 touched packages, make boundary-guard (0 escape hatches) and openspec validate --strict were ASSISTANT-RUN and clean. The full suite (go test ./internal/telemetry/... ./internal/app/... ./internal/analytics/... ./internal/charging/...) was run and reported PASSING by the OWNER. Judge test quality by READING the tests - do not run them. PERFORMANCE-PROFILE (verbatim): read-heavy - read performance is mandatory over write performance; writes are mostly done by pollers at midnight, so denormalizing, indexing aggressively, and precomputing for reads is acceptable - never at the cost of the modular-monolith boundaries or module data ownership. (This tier changes no query, so any performance delta is a finding.)
